newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industrial activity seen slower in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industrial activity seen slower in 2nd half.

text.p: Brazilian industry will show strong growth in the second quarter, though it is unlikely to repeat its performance in the second half of the year, the National Industry Federation (CNI) said in a statement.
The CNI based its forecast on stronger-than-expected results in April, when Brazilian industry showed a 3.5 percent rise in output and a 13.12 percent increase in sales, excluding seasonal factors.
"Although expected, the numbers were surprising in the intensity of growth shown," it said.
Howver, the April figures should not be taken as a sign the economy is overheating, but rather as the result of favorable factors that are unlikely to be repeated in the coming months, the CNI said.

April's strong showing reflected a greater number of working days, high demand in anticipation of possible credit-tightening moves by the government and a strong expansion in agriculture, the CNI said.

Consumption-restricting measures should have begun to reduce durable goods purchases in May. A poll showed consumers were already planning to buy less in the next three months, it said. Most consumers said an increase in prices for products bought on credit was the main reason behind their decision not to make installment purchases.
